sources.title: 7 AAC 12.250 - 7 AAC 12.290, Article 5, Nursing Facilities — Alaska Administrative Code, Alaska State Legislature (BASIS)
sources.source_date: none stated in the print rendering
sources.notes: Captured from the Legislature's own BASIS application endpoint rather than from its pages. The page address, akleg.gov/basis/aac.asp, is a scripted client that loads section text by GET request to this same script with media=print and a secStart/secEnd range; the request carries no session token, query hash or build identifier, so it is a stable public endpoint and is admitted as first-party under the API rule in PROVENANCE.md. This range is the whole nursing-facility article of the licensing chapter. It is captured to establish, in the state's own text, that the licensing rule states no grounds, notice period or appeal route for a facility-initiated transfer or discharge; the page records that as a finding. The endpoint returns an HTML fragment with no html or body element, a single div.statute wrapping the requested sections; the scope names that div.

sources.title: 7 AAC 12.890, Rights of patients, clients, and residents — Alaska Administrative Code, Alaska State Legislature (BASIS)
sources.source_date: none stated in the print rendering
sources.notes: Same endpoint and same admission as source 1. The general rights section of the licensing chapter, which applies to nursing facilities; captured for the same reason, as the second place a state-stated ground or notice period would sit if the licensing rule carried one. The endpoint returns an HTML fragment with no html or body element, a single div.statute wrapping the requested sections; the scope names that div.

sources.title: 7 AAC 140.540 - 7 AAC 140.585, Nursing Facility Services (transfer, discharge, absence from nursing facility) — Alaska Administrative Code, Alaska State Legislature (BASIS)
sources.source_date: none stated in the print rendering
sources.notes: Same endpoint and same admission as source 1. The Medicaid coverage rule for nursing facilities: 7 AAC 140.540 (transfer of recipients, ten-day written notice, hearing under 7 AAC 49), 7 AAC 140.545 (discharge of recipients, same), and 7 AAC 140.585 (payment for reserving a bed during a planned absence, and none during hospitalization). The range also carries the intervening sections on payment and personal funds; a superset only adds evidence. The endpoint returns an HTML fragment with no html or body element, a single div.statute wrapping the requested sections; the scope names that div.

sources.title: 7 AAC 49.010 - 7 AAC 49.200, Hearings — Alaska Administrative Code, Alaska State Legislature (BASIS)
sources.source_date: none stated in the print rendering
sources.notes: Same endpoint and same admission as source 1. The hearing chapter that 7 AAC 140.540(c) and 140.545(b) send a recipient to: 7 AAC 49.030 (request in writing to the department within 30 days; referral to the office of administrative hearings), 7 AAC 49.060 (ten-day notice of proposed agency action) and 7 AAC 49.190 (continuation of assistance while a hearing is pending). The endpoint returns an HTML fragment with no html or body element, a single div.statute wrapping the requested sections; the scope names that div.

sources.title: Uni-08, Notice of Recipient Fair Hearing Rights — Alaska Department of Health (PDF)
sources.source_date: Revised 2/1/2025, as the form's footer states
sources.notes: The department's own hearing-rights notice and request form, listed on its Approved SDS Forms page (source 6). It is the one Alaska source that prints where a fair hearing request is sent: a mailing address, fax, email and telephone, all routed through the department's fiscal agent. The form's columnar layout renders address, fax, email and telephone on shared lines; quotations are taken as the capture renders them.

sources.title: Approved SDS Forms — Division of Senior and Disabilities Services, Alaska Department of Health
sources.notes: The department page that lists source 5 by name (Uni-08 Fair Hearing Rights Notice) among the division's approved forms. Captured so the form's standing as a department instrument rests on the department's own listing rather than on a file address.
